intended_object: For a graded R-algebra A = ⨁ᵢ 𝒜ᵢ, the R-linear projection A → A that sends a to its degree-i homogeneous component aᵢ (viewed back in A). Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body takes a ∈ A, decomposes it with `decomposeAlgEquiv 𝒜` (A ≃ₐ ⨁ᵢ 𝒜ᵢ), evaluates at i with `DFinsupp.lapply i`, and includes the result back into A with `(𝒜 i).subtype`. So a ↦ (decompose a i : A). This is exactly the degree-i projection, as an R-linear map; `GradedAlgebra.proj_apply` states the same formula. It is the R-linear version of `GradedRing.proj`, which is only an additive monoid hom. It is stated for graded algebras, which is the setting its name and docstring give. The same construction would also work for any `DirectSum.Decomposition` of a module into submodules (via `decomposeLinearEquiv`), but that is a different, more general notion and not what this declaration is meant to be. Nothing is wrong in degenerate cases either.
